_comment: Routing config only — endpoint, model id, reasoning effort, profile membership. Carries NO quality scores: a stale ranking is worse than none. Availability is MEASURED by `review.py --list`, which probes each provider live; a key being set is not availability. All reviewers use DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (64000) unless they set max_output_tokens: reasoning tokens come out of the answer's budget, and at 16000 a large review returned no content at all. Prices in _cost are per million tokens as listed 2026-08-25 and are a budgeting hint, not a routing input.

_profiles.plan: TWO contrasting models, never escalated. For acceptance criteria and designs, BEFORE code exists. A third reviewer adds agreement, not insight.
_profiles.fast: cheapest implementation panel; the first tier of --escalate
_profiles.standard: fast + mid-cost; the usual implementation panel
_profiles.deep: standard + astra. Final --escalate tier, or a fixed --profile deep panel. sol is NOT here: it writes the code now, and an author does not review itself.
_profiles.committee: committee.py members. SEPARATE from the gate profiles on purpose: deepseek plans and concedes well but over-claims as a refuter, so it sits here and in no gate profile.

reviewers.name: kimi-k2.7-code
reviewers._effort: null is measured, not forgotten; see _effort_null_is_deliberate

reviewers.name: sol
reviewers._note: deep-tier reviewer AND tie-breaker: the ladder reaches deep both when the cheaper tiers came up clean and when they could not fill quorum, and skips it only when a finding already has quorum behind it.

reviewers.name: kimi-k3
reviewers._note: dropped 2026-08-27: $15.00/M output, dearer than sol ($10.00) which is the deep-only tie-breaker, so cheapest-first reached its priciest reviewer before its designated last resort. Disabled rather than deleted so the reason survives; flip enabled to re-add.

reviewers.name: glm-5.3
reviewers._note: 1M context, so it does not need the >100KB review split. glm-5.2 is marginally cheaper (1.19/3.74) with the same context if cost matters more than recency.
reviewers._effort: null is measured, not forgotten; see _effort_null_is_deliberate

_effort_null_is_deliberate: Measured 2026-09-19, three samples per cell against a real 120-line diff at a 16000 cap: glm-5.3 at effort=high burned the ENTIRE budget on reasoning and returned zero characters in 3 of 3 samples, at effort=low in 2 of 3, and at effort=null returned a 4581-character review for $0.016 in 3 of 3. kimi-k2.7-code spends ~12k completion tokens at every level, so effort changes nothing but price: high cost 83% more and returned slightly LESS answer. A null effort here is therefore deliberate and load-bearing, not an omission. Setting one on either reviewer makes the gate pay more for less, and on glm-5.3 for nothing at all.
